text:
Maya: Quick sync — postmortem is done, and we need a short external follow-up for customers + the statuspage blurb. Two decisions: (1) who owns the customer-facing 72h summary, (2) do we publish a redacted RCA or only an external summary. @Kevin @Emily can you own statuspage + customer note respectively?
Kevin: I can take statuspage. I’ll draft a succinct message and post here by EOD. Do we have the condensed timeline I can reference?
Raj: Timeline is in the postmortem doc but TL;DR I’ll paste the compact version below.
Raj: ```
- 11:23 UTC: elevated inference latency detected (autoscaling didn't kick immediately)
- 11:51 UTC: mitigation applied (routing tweak + scale-up)
- 12:10 UTC: traffic normalized, KV cache warmed, full recovery confirmed
- Root cause: race in scale-up + cache warm path under bursty traffic
```
Emily: I’ll own the 72h customer note. Plan: 3 short paragraphs — what happened, who was impacted, what we did + next steps. Question: do we link to the full RCA or only a customer-friendly summary?
Maya: My recommendation: publish a redacted RCA summary publicly (no internal timelines, stack traces, or customer IDs). Make the full RCA available to enterprise customers/support on request. Keeps transparency but avoids sensitive details.
Kevin: Draft statuspage suggestion: "We experienced intermittent inference latency affecting API response times between ~11:23–12:10 UTC. The issue caused increased error rates and slower responses for a subset of requests. Mitigation was applied and normal service resumed at ~12:10 UTC. A follow-up customer note and investigation summary will be available within 72 hours." Short, factual, links to the 72h note. Thoughts?
Emily: That reads well. For the 72h note I'll include: impact metrics (requests affected %), mitigation steps, temporary workarounds, permanent remediation plan, and owners+ETA for fixes.
Incident Bot: Reminder — add owner tags to the postmortem actions: /assign @Emily for external note, /assign @Kevin for statuspage, /assign @Raj for timeline artifacts.
Maya: OK, final action list (compact):
1) Statuspage blurb (Kevin) — draft in thread by 2024-06-14 17:00 UTC (owner: Kevin)
2) 72h customer note (Emily) — first draft by 2024-06-15 16:00 UTC, final by 2024-06-17 16:00 UTC (owner: Emily)
3) Timeline + sanitized artifacts (Raj) — push sanitized timeline + key logs to postmortem doc by 2024-06-14 20:00 UTC (owner: Raj)
4) RCA sharing policy for this incident (Maya) — recommend redacted public summary + full RCA on request; finalize wording by 2024-06-15 12:00 UTC (owner: Maya)
5) Recurring-patterns check (SRE/Raj + Eng) — quick check to see if this aligns with past burst-related cache issues; short report by 2024-06-18 (owner: Raj)
Kevin: :thumbsup: I’ll drop the statuspage text in 30m and link to Emily’s note when ready.
Emily: I’ll post a first-pass doc to the thread tomorrow morning and request reviews.
Maya: Thanks — once everything is linked, we’ll update the statuspage with the note link and close the follow-up loop.
Kevin: One more ask — include the simplest customer-facing mitigation line: "We have deployed a fix to ensure prompt autoscaling + improved cache warm paths." Keep it high-level.
Maya: Agreed. Keep the customer language simple, no internal detail.
Emily: Noted. I’ll also add an FAQ entry for common customer questions (rate limits, retries, enterprise support).
Incident Bot: Action items recorded: 5 owners assigned. If any ETA slips, please update the postmortem status.
